steps.title: Look at the phrases again.
steps.sub: I’m afraid I can’t make the 28th. How about the 29th instead?
steps.prompt: Why does the speaker add “How about the 29th instead?”
options: Saying no is not enough — you offer another day.
Because the 28th is impossible for everyone.
steps.answer: Saying no is not enough — you offer another day.
steps.why: In English, a refusal is normally followed by an alternative. Otherwise it sounds like the end of the conversation.

steps.title: Inviting and arranging
steps.html:
What you are doingWhat you say
checking they are freeAre you free that week at all? / Are you doing anything on Friday?
invitingWould you like to meet for lunch? / Do you fancy doing something?
acceptingThat’d be lovely. / Sounds great! / That works for me.
refusing politelyI’m afraid I can’t make the 28th. / Sorry, I can’t make it.
suggesting another dayHow about the 29th instead? / Is Sunday any good for you?
fixing the detailsShall we meet outside the restaurant at eight? / Shall we say half past seven?

Do you fancy and How about are followed by the -ing form or a noun: Do you fancy doing something? How about Friday?

Would you like to and Shall we are followed by the base form: Would you like to meet? Shall we say eight?

I’m afraid makes a refusal polite. Always follow it with an alternative.

Can’t make it = cannot come. I can’t make Friday is normal, everyday English.

You will use I’m afraid again in Unit 7, Lesson 21, when something is wrong with a hotel room.

steps.title: Arrangement email · model
steps.html:
The same arrangement, written as an email. You will write your own at the end.

Changing the day and fixing the details

Subject: Thursday — confirming

Hi Dana,

Thanks for your message. Do you fancy having dinner on Thursday instead of Wednesday? I’m afraid I can’t make Wednesday — I’m working late.

How about the new Georgian place on the seafront? Shall we say half past seven? If that’s too early, eight works for me too.

I’m going to book a table this evening, so let me know by six if you can.

See you Thursday,

Aisulu

steps.title: Write an email arranging to meet someone.
steps.sub: About 80–110 words. Follow the model: invite, refuse the first day politely, suggest another, fix the time, ask for an answer.
steps.html:
1. Plan (from the model): greeting → the invitation → the day you can’t make and why → the day you suggest → the place and the time → what you need from them → sign-off.
  • Hi …,
  • Do you fancy …ing on …?
  • I’m afraid I can’t make … — I’m …
  • How about … instead?
  • Shall we say …?
  • Let me know by …
  • See you …,
Do you fancyWould you like toI’m afraid I can’t makeHow aboutinsteadShall we sayThat works for meLet me knowI’m going to bookSee you
steps.modelHtml:
• I began with a greeting and ended with a sign-off.
  • I used an invitation phrase from the Useful language box.
  • I refused one day politely and suggested another.
  • I fixed a place and a time.
  • I used one future form for what I am going to do.
